title: Evaluating the Association Between Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Reduction and Relative and Absolute Effects of Statin Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
authors: Byrne P, Demasi M, Jones M, Smith SM, O'Brien KK, DuBroff R
population: 21 randomised trials of statin against placebo or usual care with at least 1000 participants and planned duration of 2 years or more: 7 primary prevention, 6 secondary prevention and 8 mixed; 1255 to 20,536 participants per trial
funder: not stated; the article information lists no funding source
result: Absolute risk reductions with statins: all-cause mortality 0.8% (95% CI 0.4% to 1.2%), myocardial infarction 1.3% (0.9% to 1.7%), stroke 0.4% (0.2% to 0.6%), with relative risk reductions of 9%, 29% and 14%; in primary prevention trials the absolute reductions were 0.6%, 0.7% and 0.3%, and in secondary prevention 0.9%, 2.2% and 0.7%. About 77 people would need treatment for about 4.4 years to prevent one myocardial infarction. Meta-regression of outcome on the magnitude of LDL cholesterol reduction was inconclusive. All included trials were funded in part or wholly by the pharmaceutical industry; heterogeneity was significant.
